analytic.title: Supporting Hard Real-time Communication of Periodic Messages over Switched Ethernet

div.p: Nowadays, switched Ethernet is considered as an attractive enabling technology for supporting industrial communication needs. However, because of some disadvantages, switched Ethernet requires some mechanisms for supporting real- time communication, which is the most important challenge in industrial communication. This paper suggests and proves the schedulability condition for hard real-time periodic messages on a switched Ethernet that are scheduled under EDF-based scheduling algorithm without any modification of original switches, thus they can be applied directly to industrial communication. The switched Ethernet operates based on the master-slaves principles and the synchronized model, and the transmission of real-time periodic messages will be handled by master node to fulfill their hard real-time requirements.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: In recent years, switched Ethernet has been considered such as the most attractive solution for supporting real-time communication in industrial communication. Switches have many advantages such as large bandwidth, VLAN support, prioritized frame transmission, full-duplex links. Unlike traditional, shared Ethernet, switched Ethernet provides a private collision domain for each of its ports and promises to support real-time communication. However, because of some reasons, original switches can not be applied directly to industrial communication. The main disadvantage of switched Ethernet is the collision of messages at the output port. When two or more messages are destined to the same output port at the same time, they are first stored in the output buffer and after that, are transmitted one by one to the output link, and message loss may occur in the case of output buffer overflow. The second disadvantage is that the standard switch uses FIFO (First-in-First-out) queuing where the messages with higher priorities may have to wait in the queue while the lower priority messages are being transmitted. These situations affect strongly the real-time communication over switched Ethernet.

This paper analyzes schedulability condition and proposes a EDF-based real-time message scheduling algorithm for periodic messages over switched Ethernet that operates based on master-slaves principle and the synchronized model. The master node checks whether the messages can meet their deadline or not (admission control) and dynamically schedules for real-time periodic traffic over switched Ethernet and there is no need to modify the original FIFO queue on switches. The rest of paper is organized as follows. In section 2, the previous works on industrial switched Ethernet are described. Section 3 describes the schedulability condition for EDF scheduling of real-time messages and proposes the real-time message scheduling algorithm for periodic messages over switched Ethernet. Section 4 concludes and summaries the paper.

div.head: II. RELATED WORKS
div.p: From the last few years, a large number of works have been done to analyze the applicability of switched Ethernet to industrial communication. The first idea was using Network Calculus theory for evaluating the real-time performance of switched Ethernet networks. George [01] presented a method to design the architectures of switched Ethernet networks which aimed to minimize end-to-end delays by using Network Calculus theory. This method may be effective when designing static applications to guarantee real-time performance of switched Ethernet networks. Another work has been done by Loser and Hartig [2], where they used the traffic shaper (smoother) to regulate the traffic entering switched Ethernet and to bound end-to-end delay based on Network Calculus theory [3]. In this method, the traffic pattern must satisfy the burstiness constraints to guarantee the delay bounds to be met. Another way to support real-time communication is modifying the original switches to have extra functionality to provide more efficient scheduling policy and admission control. Hoai Hoang [04] attempted to support real-time communication over switched Ethernet by adding the real-time layer in both end nodes and a switch. Instead of using FIFO queuing, packets are queued in the order of deadline in the switch. A source node, before sending a real-time periodic message to the destination node, has to establish a real-time channel that is controlled by the switch for guaranteeing the deadline. M. K. Kim [5] proposed a distributed scheduling algorithm of periodic messages for hard real-time communications on a switched Ethernet without modifying the operation of the standard switch. However, they did not show the feasibility condition of periodic messages on the switched Ethernet.

div.head: REAL-TIME MESSAGE SCHEDULING OF PERIODIC MESSAGES OVER SWITCHED ETHERNET
div.p: In this section, we describe a schedulability condition for EDF scheduling of periodic messages and propose a real-time message scheduling algorithm based on EDF scheduling that was first introduced by Liu and Layland [6]. The switched Ethernet operates in master-slave mode and uses a synchronized message transmission model. The master node handles the transmission of periodic message to guarantee the timeliness of all the periodic messages.

A. Network Architecture We assume that the switched Ethernet operates in full-suplex mode,where each node is connected to the switch through a pair of links: a transmission link (TL) and a reception link (RL). One of the nodes acts as a master to handle the real-time communication of periodic messages. The real-time layer is added to all end nodes to enhance the real-time performance of switched Ethernet (Fig. 1). Moreover, we assume that the switch operates in cut-through mode to minimize the switch latency of the messages when they are transmitted over switched Ethernet (for further details see subsection III-B) The operation of real-time communication network can be described as follows. Firstly, all the slave nodes send the real- time requirements to the master node. After receiving all the request frames from slaves, the master node checks the feasibility of the synchronous messages (admission control) and broadcasts the result to all the slaves to indicate which messages can be transmitted over the switched Ethernet and meet their deadline. The real-time periodic messages, when arriving at slave nodes, are sorted in the increasing order of their deadline at the real-time layer. Then a master node periodically broadcasts a trigger message to all slave nodes to synchronize the communication system and to indicate a set of messages to be transmitted.

div.head: B. Message Transmission Model
div.p: In this paper, we assume that all nodes operate in the synchronized model, which is similar to that of FTT-CAN [7]. All the transmission and reception links are slotted into a sequence of fundamental time units, called Elementary Cycles (ECs). An EC consists of a TM, a SMP (Synchronous Message Period) and a AMP (Asynchronous Message Period) as shown in Fig. 2-(a). In this paper, we only consider the scheduling of periodic messages, so for the simplicity of the analysis, we assume there is no AMP in each EC as shown in Fig. 2-(b). The TM (Trigger Message) is used to synchronize all nodes and contains a schedule for the periodic messages that can be transmitted on the respective EC. The SMP and the AMP are the time durations for transmitting real-time periodic messages and aperiodic messages on the EC, respectively. div.head: V. CONCLUSIONS AND FUTURE WORKS
div.p: Real-time distributed control systems have been more widely used in industrial applications like process control, factory automation, vehicles, etc. In the last decade, the interest of using Ethenet switches in industrial communications has been growing as a means to improve global throughput, traffic isolation, and reduce the impact of the nondeterministic features of the CSMA/CD arbitration mechanism. However, it needs some mechanisms to regulate the traffic on the network in order to satisfy the hard real-time communication requirements of industrial applications. In this paper, the EDF- based scheduling algorithm for hard real-time communication over switched Ethernet was proposed. With this scheduling algorithm, there is no need to modify the original principles of switches to support hard real-time communication in industrial environment. This paper also analyzed the schedulability condition for EDF scheduling of real-time periodic messages and showed that the proposed scheduling algorithm reflects correctly the feasibility condition of the periodic messages on the switched Ethernet. We will analyze the real-time features of aperiodic messages as well as the level of flexibility of the proposed scheduling algorithm in the future.
